newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries dip slightly in quiet London market.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries dip slightly in quiet London market.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were steady to lower in London on Wednesday in thin volumes, said traders, adding they anticipated little impact from U.S. data due later.
They said the industrial production and housing starts figures would be largely neutral for the market, after Tuesday's relatively modest consumer price numbers pushed bonds higher in New York.

"We've had a quiet session following on from what we saw in Tokyo overnight and we haven't really been able to build much on the gains seen yesterday in New York after the CPI figures," said Rob Hayward, economic adviser at BankAmerica in London.
At 0953 GMT the 30-year long bond was at 94-05 to yield 7.10 percent, down from 94-09 in Tokyo and 94-07 in New York.

The two-year benchmark was at 99-21, yielding 6.44 percent unchanged from both Tokyo and New York, while 10-year T-notes were at 95-17 to yield 6.88 percent, unchanged from Tokyo and versus 95-18 at Tuesday's New York close.

"There is almost nothing going on," said a Treasuries trader at a U.S. bank in London. "We've had lower than average volume after a decent volume day yesterday, and we're trading in a very tight range."
According to a Reuters poll, March housing starts, due at 1230 GMT, are seen at 1.46 million, compared with 1.528 million in February.
March industrial production, released at 1315 GMT, is seen up 0.6 percent versus a 0.5 percent rise previously. Capacity utilisation is seen at 83.6 percent, compared with 83.3 percent in February.
The trader said housing starts would not be as influential as industrial production and capacity utilisation.

"The market is expecting pretty healthy gains and that is what we will have to watch for," he said. "CPI has turned sentiment to the positive side, and if those numbers come in weaker than expected we could see further moves to the upside."
He said 7.0 percent would be fairly strong resistance on the long bond.
Hayward said the data was likely to be neutral overall.

"Today's numbers will paint a fairly mixed picture," he said. "The risk is if we don't get a slow down in housing, or if we get slightly stronger industrial production figures which push capactity utilisation towards the 84 percent level...we might have a slightly neagative bias in the market."
The 84 percent level for capacity utilisation is usually associated with inflationary pressures, Hayward said.
"But apart from that, we are probably in for a bit of a consolidative tone until we get through to the employment cost index which is out on April 29," he said.
June T-bond futures were at 107-20, steady in automated trade.
